g12-economics-ue3-t1.overview: Market Failure sits inside Market Failure and Consumer Protection. Market failure is the focus of Unit 3 of Grade 12 Economics in the Ethiopian (FDRE Ministry of Education) curriculum. First, it defines market failure and its common types. Then it explains public goods and their features. Next, it covers externalities and asymmetric information. Finally, it turns to consumer protection. Students will also learn how market failure calls for real-life government action.
objectives: Define market failure and identify its causes.
State the characteristics of public goods.
Explain externalities and asymmetric information.
Describe the main solutions, from taxes to regulation.
Explain the meaning of consumer protection.
g12-economics-ue3-t1.simple:
Market Failure in plain words. The exam wants you to recognise the core ideas, not to memorise whole paragraphs. Focus on:
  • First, an inefficient allocation of resources when markets fail.
  • Then its common types.
  • Also the possible solutions, including government action.
g12-economics-ue3-t1.detailed:
Market Failure — the essentials. First, an inefficient allocation of resources when markets fail. Then its common types. Also the possible solutions, including government action.

What the MoE expects you to be able to do:

  • Define market failure and identify its causes.
  • State the characteristics of public goods.
  • Explain externalities and asymmetric information.
  • Describe the main solutions, from taxes to regulation.
  • Explain the meaning of consumer protection.

keyTerms.def: First, an inefficient allocation of resources when markets fail.
Also the possible solutions, including government action.
